9. In deciding Issue Nos. 4 and 5 Learned Assistant Judge held that Plaintiff filed certified Copies of Heba-Bil-Ewaz Deeds dated 29.10.1948 and 30.10.1948 and Plaintiff proved those two Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds in accordance with Law. Learned Assistant Judge further held that in accordance with Section 60 of Registration Act Ownership of Property conveyed by Two Heba-Bil-Ewaz. Deeds dated 29.10.1948 and 30.10.1948 (Exhibit 2 and 2 (ha) respectively) vested upon Plaintiff. Learned Assistant Judge, also, held that Plaintiff filed State Acquisition khatian which has been exhibited as Exhibit ka (K) and presumption of Law is that S.A. Khatian having been prepared in the name of Plaintiff, Plaintiff was found in possession on Suit Property during the period of preparation S.A. Khatian. Learned Assistant-Judge, also, rendered decision that from evidence, both documentary and oral it became manifestly clear that Plaintiff by way of two Deeds dated 29.10.1948 and 30.10.1948 became owner and possessor of Suit Property. In rendering decision Learned Assistant Judge duly considered evidence of P.WS 1, 3 and 4 who are tenants under Plaintiff since the year 1967-1968 and Defendant side could not bring out any sort of contradiction in versions supplied by P.W.s. Learned Assistant Judge, also, came to hold that Defendant failed to prove that Notice of Requisition and Acquisition had been served upon Plaintiff. Learned Assistant Judge taking into account provision embodied in Section. 4 of (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act 1948 and, also provisions contained in Section 7 of Act of 1948 and Section B and Sub-Section B and Section C and, also, relevant sections of Ordinance No. IX of 1969 held that Plaintiff having proved his ownership and possession on Suit Property is entitled to get reliefs prayed for. 

 18. The Point now may be discussed and answered. Exhibit 2 and 2 (ka) are two registered Heba-Bil-Ewaz Deeds dated 29.10.1948 and 30.10.1948 with respect to suit property i.e. 0.17 acres + 0.17 acres = 0.34 acres from C.S. Plot No. 1356 corresponding to S.A. Plot No. 4017 and 4019 and those two Heba-Bil-Ewan Deeds had been lawfully proved by Plaintiff by calling volumes of Deeds Exhibit I. Slate Acquisition Khatian prepared in the name of Plaintiff and there is presumption of correctness of the Record of Right, that is, S.A. Khatian prepared in the name of Plaintiff and this Presumption is attached under section 144 A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It appears that Defendant-Petitioner did neither deny existence of two Heba-Bil-Ewan Deeds nor take any steps against the Deeds. Plaintiff-Opposite Party No. 1 in order to prove the Deeds examined himself as P.W.1 and put on witness box PW-2, Deed Writer of two Heba-Bil-Ewaz Deeds who proved two Hcba-Bil-Ewaz Deeds which had been exhibited as Exhibit 2 and 2 (ka) and, also, PW-5 and PW-6 who being employees of Office of District Registrar brought volumes of two Deeds. Plaintiff-Opposite Party examined PW-3 and PW-4 to prove his Possession on suit property. PW-3 stated in his evidence that Plaintiff is the Owner and Possessor of Suit Property and on suit property there are three "Pucca" Houses and Twelve Thatched Houses and a Shop and Plaintiff possessed those through tenants. PW-3 stated that he constructed Ration Shop on Suit Properly and he is a tenant under Plaintiff. PW-4 in his evidence stated that on the suit homestead he is a tenant in two rooms under Plaintiff and he has been in the homestead since the Year 1967-1968 and Plaintiff inducted many persons on suit property as tenants and in all there are 20-25 tenants on suit property under Plaintiff. PW-5 is Record Keeper of the Office of District Registrar, Dhaka and he came to Court with Volumes and he proved the Deed dated 30.10.1948 which was exhibited as Exhibit 2 (ka). PW-6 in his evidence stated that he carried Volumes from the office of District Registrar. Dhaka and proved Deed dated 29/10/1948 and the said Deed had been exhibited as Exhibit-2. Credibility of evidences of PW-1, PW-2, PW-3, PW-4, PW-5 and PW-6 could not be shattered by way of cross examination from the side of Defendant- Petitioner.
